**Day Panel is now Daybook** — it grew a money tab, and a name about one panel no longer fit. Your data carries straight over: it lives in its own folder, which kept its original name so that no rename could ever lose it.

## New

- **Money.** Write down what you spend in two taps — a category, an amount, Enter. See it by day, week, month or year: the total, how it compares to before, a ring showing where it went, bars for the periods before, and a category-by-category comparison with any earlier period ("Food 33% less, Going out 18% more"). While a month is still running it is compared with last month *up to the same date*, not with the whole of it. There is example data to try it with, and one button takes it out again.
- **A Mac version.** One file for every Mac, Intel or Apple silicon.
- **Updates from inside the app.** When a newer version is out, a button appears in the panel and on the widget. On Windows with the installer it downloads and installs; the portable exe and the Mac version open the download page.
- **Fill in any day where you fill in today.** Press a day on the calendar and the habit tiles, tasks and note all become that day's, edited the same way. No separate card any more.
- **Pin the widget to the desktop** (Settings → Desktop widget): out of the taskbar and Alt+Tab, behind your windows, back after "show desktop".

## Changed

- The clock shows hours and minutes, no seconds.
- The greeting changes every day of the week.
- No File / Edit / View menu bar on Windows.

## Fixed

- The unit field under *Add your own* looked dead: its hint sat centred in the box and read like text that would not delete.
- The time field for the daily reminder always fell back to 21:00.

## Downloading

- **Windows:** `Daybook-Setup-1.1.0.exe` (installs, and updates itself from now on) or `Daybook-1.1.0-portable.exe` (runs without installing). Windows will say *"Windows protected your PC"* — press **More info → Run anyway**.
- **Mac:** `Daybook-1.1.0-mac.dmg`. The first time, macOS refuses to open it; go to **System Settings → Privacy & Security** and press **Open Anyway** next to Daybook.

Both warnings are about the missing paid signing certificates, not about the program. The source is all in this repository if you would rather build it yourself.
